title: Nscale Banks on US Data Center Project to Justify $35B IPO Target
summary:
The London-based AI infrastructure provider is seeking to raise the market price for its upcoming public debut as it expands its operations into the United States. Nscale is now targeting a $35 billion valuation for its planned initial public offering on a US exchange, an increase from earlier goals of $30 billion, relying on the growth of a vast Texas data center project to justify the pricing despite financing risks and local opposition.

The company's founder and CEO, Josh Payne, transitioned the firm from a small cryptocurrency mining operation into a 'neocloud' business that borrows heavily to purchase chips and build facilities. This growth is heavily supported by Nvidia, which has provided more than $1.17 billion in equity funding and lease guarantees to help the company manage about $24 billion in outstanding equipment commitments for 2026 and 2027.

selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
Nscale, which filed its S-1 and is looking to start its roadshow soon, is a former lessor of data center infrastructure to crypto mining companies that de facto made the shift to AI by 2025. Nscale, leasing and operating dozens of MWs only, with dozens of millions in revenue, has big dreams. Luckily for Nscale, it was adopted by a very rich Uncle, whose name is Jensen.

Jensen adopted the very micro neocloud, which had basically only one customer in 2024, as NVIDIA’s very own SPV.

NVIDIA has invested over $1.17B in the Series B and C funding rounds, owning approx. 18% of Nscale as an investor (but with 0% of the voting power so it won’t appear in holders table)

Besides that, NVIDIA has committed another $1B out of $3.1B in convertible loan notes, which will convert into shares in the upcoming IPO.

NVIDIA has provided a backstop PO worth $1.2B over a term of 12-48 months, and a lease guarantee of up to $860M for Nscale’s facility in Ward County, Texas.

NVIDIA has been matchmaking Microsoft, Figure AI and possibility of Anthropic in order to inflate Nscale’s RPO, which less than 2 years ago was not even $1B, and to boost IPO pricing.

NVIDIA has a very big reason for all of that. Nscale has $24B worth of outstanding equipment commitments (NVIDIA systems) for 2026 and 2027.

To pay for that, so NVIDIA will get these $24B worth of POs, they need this IPO.

And that’s just the tip of the iceberg of what is called Nscale.

An article, as part of “The Neoclouds Series”, is coming soon.
